name: Oxybutynin
route_note: Oral immediate- or extended-release tablets; twice-weekly transdermal patch; daily topical gel
rx_status: prescription; patch OTC for women in the US
tagline: Classic antimuscarinic for overactive bladder, now in patches and gels
summary: Oxybutynin is an antimuscarinic drug that relaxes the bladder detrusor muscle, reducing urgency, frequency and urge incontinence. It is effective and inexpensive but its anticholinergic effects, especially dry mouth and possible cognitive harm in older adults, limit use.
mechanism: Bladder contraction is triggered by acetylcholine acting mainly on M3 muscarinic receptors in the detrusor. Oxybutynin competitively blocks these receptors (with M1 activity), increasing bladder capacity and reducing involuntary contractions.

It also has direct smooth-muscle relaxant and local anaesthetic properties. Its active metabolite N-desethyloxybutynin, formed by gut and liver CYP3A4, contributes to dry mouth; transdermal delivery bypasses first-pass metabolism and produces less of it.
uses: Overactive bladder with urge incontinence, urgency and frequency
Detrusor overactivity in neurological conditions such as spina bifida (children)

history.title: Extended release
history.detail: FDA approves Ditropan XL once-daily tablets.

history.title: Transdermal patch
history.detail: FDA approves Oxytrol, a twice-weekly oxybutynin patch.

history.title: First OTC bladder drug
history.detail: Oxytrol for Women becomes the first over-the-counter treatment for overactive bladder in the US.

history.title: Dementia association
history.detail: A large cohort study links cumulative anticholinergic use, including bladder antimuscarinics, with increased dementia risk.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic and gut-wall CYP3A4 to active N-desethyloxybutynin

serious: Cognitive impairment and confusion in older adults

facts: Oxybutynin is listed in the Beers Criteria among strongly anticholinergic drugs best avoided in older adults.
Transdermal and gel formulations produce less N-desethyloxybutynin than oral tablets, which reduces dry mouth.
